The old centroid-centered contractions of common factor exist by support convergence and positive centroidal inradii. Pushing each row preserves its base barycenter and the pushed barycenter lies in the actual p_i fiber by convexity of the canonical hull. Interior limits keep the new marks interior, with no need for the fiberwise map to preserve compatibility as a map of bodies.

Below the atomic value, at the larger of two positive scalar inputs the attained minimizing cap is own-proper. Decreasing its scalar raises the threshold, removing strictly positive own mass near the proper section, hence strict scalar growth holds. At zero the old value is strictly below Q by that same comparison; saturation at large scalar is the whole-own-fiber case. Fixed-scalar all-tilt continuity brackets Q uniformly, and a bracketing argument gives convergence of inverses and a common H_t range about zero.

The pushed Jensen bound uses the tilted probability row, followed by log Jensen in its L/L_i reweighting. The original-volume mixture is dm/M and the common continuous Jacobian j_t gives the collar identity with the minus sign. Zero-extended log convergence and collar volume going to zero imply ξ_t→0. The scalar values of every pushed mark lie at most at the inverse evaluated at q_t, giving H_t(q_t)≥ξ_t.

An assumed upward excess at a limiting boundary point is excluded by extending the segment from a fixed interior point and applying concavity before letting its fraction tend to one. Reference values have a common positive floor, so the upper log comparison gives an o(h_t) integrated error of the correct sign. Strictly increasing B_i is also uniformly upper Lipschitz in log s on its compact scalar range, so its inverse gives the asserted lower slope of H_t.

The actual radial collar width is a_t−b_z,t≥0. Its Jacobian (1−s)^(d−1)H_z gives the width coefficient cH_z−v_z for the positive collar integral, and the minus in ξ_t gives v_z−cH_z. Bounded displacement and compact continuity permit dominated convergence, also for endpoint counting. The separate inverse expansion then brackets q_t from below at Q+tr for any r<(c_0−B_0)/A_0, and normalizing by M_t gives the displayed +βD term.
